artifacts.summary: Sites the lean_goal empty-goals trust-surface caveat in mcp-tools-guide.md's lean_goal section (not metadata-trust-surfaces.md), names lean_verify on the fully-qualified name as the already-mandated cheaper-than-full-build check that covers the unknown-constant case via Lean's synthetic sorryAx error-recovery, rules out lean_diagnostic_messages (globally blocked), and flags two additional out-of-scope restatements of the false claim in README.md and lean-implementation-agent.md for planning to decide on.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/lean, lean_verify is consistently described across README.md, rules/lean4.md, and lean-implementation-agent.md as 'Axiom check + source scan; use fully qualified name'. Its axiom-check half surfaces a synthetic sorryAx that Lean's elaborator inserts on a term-elaboration error (e.g. unknown identifier) as error recovery, even when no literal 'sorry' token appears in source -- this is the mechanism that makes lean_verify a meaningful complement to lean_goal's goal-state-only view for catching an unknown-constant reference that lean_goal's empty goals_after cannot detect.

lean_diagnostic_messages is globally BLOCKED in agent-system/extensions/lean (mcp-tools-guide.md's CRITICAL section, blocked-mcp-tools.md, mcp-fallback-table.md) due to a known lean-lsp-mcp resource-contention bug -- it must never be recommended as a fallback/replacement check in new lean4 context documentation without first checking this blocklist, since it is a trap candidate that looks like the obvious diagnostic tool.

agent-system's index-entries.json carries a line_count field per entry, but it is mechanically regenerated by generate-context-line-counts.sh rather than hand-maintained; a content edit that leaves a file's indexed 'summary' text accurate does not by itself trigger the 'if the chosen siting changes a summary already recorded in index-entries.json, that file joins the scope' conditional-scope clause used in dispatch descriptions -- only a summary-text change does.
